vintage: Eurostat regional series 2000–2025 (ONS for UK population)

notes.text: Dublin and southern Ireland jump in 2015 as multinationals move intellectual property to Ireland. Much of this GDP never reaches households; the Income lens is the fairer view.
The 2008–09 financial crisis. Output falls almost everywhere; Greece, Spain and Ireland fall furthest over the next years.
Peak of the euro crisis: unemployment passes a third of the workforce in Andalucía and parts of Greece.
Ten countries join the EU in 2004, eight of them in Central and Eastern Europe. Watch their capitals climb from here.
COVID-19. Tourism regions (the Balearics, the Canaries, the Algarve) drop hardest relative to the EU average.

eu_note: GDP per person is measured in purchasing power standards relative to the EU27 average of each year (EU = 100), so inflation and exchange rates do not colour the map.
